Module 1 · Session 1.4 · 20 min

PRD, capability status and technical truth

A source-linked technical walkthrough with an executable-system perspective.

After this session, you can:
  • Use the canonical product definition
  • Distinguish implemented from production-ready
  • Find evidence for a capability claim

Technical flow

1. The PRD stack

The canonical product definition is what-we-are-building.md. The complete-system capability catalogue decomposes that intent into stable capability IDs and maturity. The journey support matrix owns public maturity for all 21 product journeys. Architecture documents explain the designed boundary; current-implementation.md explains what exists.

2. Evidence beats page presence

A screen, lesson or route is not proof of production readiness. Capability trace records connect a requirement to code, tests and documents. Live providers, tenant configuration, UAT, security, DR and witnessed operating effectiveness may still be required.

3. Change discipline

When code and a load-bearing architecture source disagree, reconcile the design explicitly. User-visible workflow changes update Guide/Academy content. Structural decisions need ADRs; decision-engine changes must map to INV, DEC and SEC obligations.
